1962.us: President Kennedy confronted the Soviet Union in the 13-day Cuban Missile Crisis in October. John Glenn became the first American to orbit Earth, and James Meredith integrated the University of Mississippi.
1962.latam: Jamaica and Trinidad and Tobago won independence from Britain in August. Brazil won the football World Cup hosted by Chile, and Cuba became the flashpoint of the missile crisis.
1962.europe: The Second Vatican Council opened in Rome in October, and the Beatles released their first single, “Love Me Do”. France signed the Évian Accords, ending its war in Algeria.
1962.russia: Soviet leader Nikita Khrushchev placed nuclear missiles in Cuba, then withdrew them. Troops shot striking workers in Novocherkassk, and Solzhenitsyn’s gulag story “One Day in the Life of Ivan Denisovich” appeared.
1962.mideast: Algeria won independence from France in July after an eight-year war. In North Yemen, officers overthrew the imam in September, starting a civil war that drew in Nasser’s Egyptian troops.
1962.africa: Uganda, Rwanda and Burundi became independent. In South Africa, Nelson Mandela was arrested in August and jailed, and the UN General Assembly called for sanctions against apartheid.
1962.india: India lost a brief border war with China in October and November, a heavy blow to Prime Minister Nehru. China declared a ceasefire and kept control of Aksai Chin.
1962.china: At the Seven Thousand Cadres Conference, Mao made a rare self-criticism over the Great Leap Forward, whose famine had killed tens of millions. Japan boomed under Prime Minister Ikeda’s income-doubling plan.

1968.us: Martin Luther King Jr. and Robert Kennedy were assassinated, and the Tet Offensive eroded support for the Vietnam War. Richard Nixon won the presidency, and Apollo 8 orbited the Moon.
1968.latam: Mexican troops fired on student protesters at Tlatelolco ten days before Mexico City hosted the Olympics. Brazil’s military regime issued AI-5, suspending civil liberties, and Peru’s army seized power.
1968.europe: Students and about 10 million striking workers paralyzed France in May. In August, Warsaw Pact troops invaded Czechoslovakia and ended Alexander Dubček’s Prague Spring reforms.
1968.russia: Leonid Brezhnev sent tanks into Czechoslovakia and claimed a right to intervene in socialist states. A handful of dissidents protested on Red Square, and Andrei Sakharov circulated an essay calling for reform.
1968.mideast: The Ba’ath Party seized power in Iraq in July, with Saddam Hussein as a rising figure. Palestinian fighters and Jordan’s army fought Israeli forces at the Battle of Karameh.
1968.africa: Images of famine in breakaway Biafra, blockaded during Nigeria’s civil war, shocked the world. Mauritius and Swaziland gained independence from Britain.
1968.india: India harvested a record wheat crop from new high-yield seeds, a breakthrough soon called the Green Revolution. The Beatles studied meditation in Rishikesh, and protests against Pakistan’s Ayub Khan began.
1968.china: Mao began sending millions of urban youths to the countryside amid the Cultural Revolution. Japan’s economy overtook West Germany’s, second only to America’s among market economies.

1973.us: The Supreme Court decided Roe v. Wade, and the last US combat troops left Vietnam. Televised Watergate hearings gripped the country, and the oil embargo brought lines at gas stations.
1973.latam: General Augusto Pinochet seized power in Chile on 11 September, and President Allende died during the coup. Uruguay’s military took over, and Juan Perón returned as Argentina’s president.
1973.europe: Britain, Ireland and Denmark joined the European Economic Community on 1 January. The oil embargo brought car-free Sundays, and Greek troops crushed a student uprising at Athens Polytechnic.
1973.russia: Leonid Brezhnev toured the United States in June at the height of détente. Moscow airlifted arms to Egypt and Syria in October, and Solzhenitsyn’s “The Gulag Archipelago” was published in Paris.
1973.mideast: Egypt and Syria attacked Israel on 6 October, starting the Yom Kippur War. Arab oil producers cut output and embargoed the US, and oil prices roughly quadrupled within months.
1973.africa: Guinea-Bissau’s rebels declared independence from Portugal months after their leader Amílcar Cabral was assassinated. A hidden famine in Ethiopia’s Wollo province was exposed on British television.
1973.india: India’s Supreme Court ruled in the Kesavananda Bharati case that Parliament cannot alter the constitution’s basic structure, and Project Tiger began. Pakistan adopted a new constitution.
1973.china: Deng Xiaoping returned from political disgrace as vice premier. In Japan, the oil shock set off panic buying of toilet paper and ended nearly two decades of rapid growth.

1975.us: New York City neared bankruptcy, and Bill Gates and Paul Allen founded Microsoft. Apollo and Soyuz spacecraft docked in orbit, and “Jaws” became the first summer blockbuster.
1975.latam: Suriname gained independence from the Netherlands in November. Military governments in South America secretly launched Operation Condor to hunt down opponents across borders.
1975.europe: Francisco Franco died in November, and Juan Carlos became king of Spain. Portugal held its first free elections in nearly 50 years, and 35 nations signed the Helsinki Accords.
1975.russia: Brezhnev signed the Helsinki Accords, gaining recognition of postwar borders in exchange for human rights pledges. Andrei Sakharov won the Nobel Peace Prize but was barred from collecting it.
1975.mideast: Lebanon’s civil war began in April. Saudi King Faisal was assassinated by a nephew, and Egypt reopened the Suez Canal, closed since the 1967 war.
1975.africa: Mozambique and Angola won independence from Portugal. Angola slid into civil war as Cuban troops and South African forces intervened on opposing sides.
1975.india: Indira Gandhi declared a state of Emergency in June, suspending civil liberties and jailing opponents. In Bangladesh, founding leader Sheikh Mujibur Rahman was assassinated in August.
1975.china: Chiang Kai-shek died in Taiwan in April. In Beijing, Zhou Enlai called for the “Four Modernizations”, while in Cambodia the Khmer Rouge seized Phnom Penh and emptied the cities.

1980.us: Mount St. Helens erupted in May, and CNN launched as the first 24-hour news channel. Ronald Reagan won the presidency while American hostages were still held in Iran.
1980.latam: Archbishop Óscar Romero was shot dead while saying Mass in El Salvador. About 125,000 Cubans left for Florida in the Mariel boatlift, and Peru’s Shining Path launched its insurgency.
1980.europe: Strikes at Gdańsk’s shipyard gave birth to Solidarity, the Soviet bloc’s first independent trade union, led by Lech Wałęsa. Yugoslavia’s leader Josip Broz Tito died in May.
1980.russia: Moscow hosted the Summer Olympics, boycotted by the US and dozens of other countries over the invasion of Afghanistan. Andrei Sakharov was exiled to the closed city of Gorky.
1980.mideast: Iraq invaded Iran in September, starting an eight-year war. Turkey’s military seized power in a coup, and American diplomats remained hostages in Tehran.
1980.africa: Zimbabwe became independent in April with Robert Mugabe as prime minister. In Liberia, Samuel Doe seized power in a coup and President William Tolbert was killed.
1980.india: Indira Gandhi returned to power in January. Her son Sanjay died in a plane crash, and India put a satellite into orbit on its own rocket for the first time.
1980.china: China made Shenzhen a special economic zone and put the Gang of Four on trial. South Korean troops crushed the Gwangju Uprising in May, and Japan released the arcade game Pac-Man.

1986.us: Space shuttle Challenger broke apart 73 seconds after launch in January, killing all seven aboard. In November, the Iran-Contra affair revealed secret arms sales to Iran under President Reagan.
1986.latam: Jean-Claude Duvalier fled Haiti in February, ending his family’s 29-year rule. Diego Maradona led Argentina to World Cup victory in Mexico, scoring the “Hand of God” goal.
1986.europe: Spain and Portugal joined the European Community in January. Swedish Prime Minister Olof Palme was shot dead in Stockholm, and Chernobyl’s fallout reached much of Europe.
1986.russia: Chernobyl’s reactor exploded in April. Mikhail Gorbachev began promoting glasnost, met Reagan at the Reykjavík summit and freed Andrei Sakharov from exile, and the Mir space station launched.
1986.mideast: US warplanes bombed Libya in April after a Berlin disco bombing that Washington blamed on Gaddafi. In the Iran-Iraq War, Iran captured Iraq’s Faw Peninsula.
1986.africa: South Africa declared a nationwide state of emergency, and the US Congress imposed sanctions over Reagan’s veto. Yoweri Museveni took power in Uganda, and Wole Soyinka won the Nobel Prize in Literature.
1986.india: Rajiv Gandhi’s government passed a law reversing the Shah Bano maintenance ruling, and a court ordered the disputed Babri Masjid unlocked. Benazir Bhutto returned to Pakistan to large crowds.
1986.china: Student protests for political reform spread from Hefei to Shanghai in December. Japan’s asset bubble began to inflate, and People Power protests drove Ferdinand Marcos from the Philippines.

1989.us: George H.W. Bush became president in January. The Exxon Valdez spilled oil into Alaska’s Prince William Sound, and an earthquake hit the San Francisco Bay Area during the World Series.
1989.latam: Riots over price hikes shook Caracas, and Paraguay’s Alfredo Stroessner was overthrown after over three decades. Chile elected its first civilian president since 1973, and US troops invaded Panama to remove Noriega.
1989.europe: Poland held partly free elections in June, and the Berlin Wall opened on 9 November. Communist rule collapsed across Eastern Europe, and Romania’s Ceaușescu was executed on Christmas Day.
1989.russia: The last Soviet troops left Afghanistan, and partly free elections produced a televised parliament of fierce debate. About two million people formed a human chain across the Baltic republics.
1989.mideast: Ayatollah Khomeini issued a fatwa against author Salman Rushdie in February and died in June. Lebanon’s factions signed the Taif Agreement, the framework for ending the civil war.
1989.africa: F.W. de Klerk became South Africa’s president and freed Walter Sisulu and other ANC leaders. Namibia voted in UN-supervised elections, and Charles Taylor’s rebels invaded Liberia.
1989.india: Rajiv Gandhi lost India’s election amid the Bofors arms scandal, and V.P. Singh became prime minister. An armed insurgency erupted in Kashmir.
1989.china: Protests in Tiananmen Square ended in a military crackdown on 4 June. In Japan, Emperor Hirohito died in January, and the stock market bubble peaked on the year’s last trading day.

1994.us: NAFTA took effect on 1 January, and millions watched O.J. Simpson’s slow-speed police chase. Republicans won both houses of Congress, taking the House for the first time in 40 years.
1994.latam: Zapatista rebels rose up in Chiapas as NAFTA began, and Mexico’s peso collapsed in December. Brazil launched the real currency to tame inflation and won the World Cup.
1994.europe: The Channel Tunnel opened between Britain and France, and the IRA declared a ceasefire. The siege of Sarajevo continued, and Norwegians voted against joining the European Union.
1994.russia: Russia’s last troops left Germany, Estonia and Latvia, and the MMM pyramid scheme collapsed, costing millions of investors their savings. In December, Boris Yeltsin sent the army into Chechnya.
1994.mideast: Yasser Arafat returned to Gaza under the Oslo Accords, and Jordan signed a peace treaty with Israel. Arafat, Yitzhak Rabin and Shimon Peres shared the Nobel Peace Prize.
1994.africa: Nelson Mandela became South Africa’s first Black president after all-race elections in April. In Rwanda, about 800,000 people, mostly Tutsi, were killed in a genocide lasting about 100 days.
1994.india: Plague broke out in Surat in September, sending hundreds of thousands fleeing the city. Indians Sushmita Sen and Aishwarya Rai won Miss Universe and Miss World as economic reforms opened the country.
1994.china: North Korea’s founder Kim Il-sung died in July, and his son Kim Jong-il took over. China connected fully to the internet and began building the Three Gorges Dam.

1996.us: Bill Clinton won re-election and signed a major welfare reform law. Atlanta hosted the Summer Olympics, marred by a bombing in Centennial Olympic Park.
1996.latam: Guatemala signed peace accords in December, ending a 36-year civil war. In Lima, Túpac Amaru rebels seized the Japanese ambassador’s residence and took hundreds of hostages.
1996.europe: Britain announced a likely link between mad cow disease and a fatal human brain illness, and the EU banned British beef exports. England hosted the Euro 96 football tournament.
1996.russia: Boris Yeltsin won re-election in a July run-off against Communist Gennady Zyuganov, despite heart trouble. The Khasavyurt agreement ended the first war in Chechnya.
1996.mideast: Benjamin Netanyahu won Israel’s first direct election for prime minister, and a truck bomb hit the Khobar Towers in Saudi Arabia. Qatar launched Al Jazeera in November.
1996.africa: South Africa adopted its post-apartheid constitution and began Truth and Reconciliation hearings. In Zaire, Laurent Kabila’s rebels, backed by Rwanda, launched the First Congo War.
1996.india: The Taliban captured Kabul. India’s Congress party lost power, Atal Bihari Vajpayee’s first government lasted 13 days, and Sri Lanka won the cricket World Cup.
1996.china: China fired test missiles near Taiwan before its first direct presidential election, which Lee Teng-hui won. In Japan, Nintendo released the first Pokémon games.

1997.us: Mars Pathfinder landed on Mars on 4 July and sent its small rover across the surface. Amazon went public, and “Titanic” opened in December on its way to becoming the top-grossing film.
1997.latam: Peruvian commandos stormed the Japanese ambassador’s residence in April, ending a four-month hostage crisis. In Mexico, the ruling PRI lost its majority in the lower house for the first time.
1997.europe: Tony Blair’s Labour Party won a landslide in Britain in May. Princess Diana died in a Paris car crash in August, and Scotland and Wales voted for devolved parliaments.
1997.russia: Boris Yeltsin signed a peace treaty with Chechnya’s leaders and the NATO-Russia Founding Act, as NATO prepared to admit former Warsaw Pact states.
1997.mideast: Reformist Mohammad Khatami won Iran’s presidential election in a landslide. In Egypt, militants killed 62 people, mostly foreign tourists, at Luxor’s Temple of Hatshepsut.
1997.africa: Laurent Kabila’s forces took Kinshasa in May, ending Mobutu Sese Seko’s 32-year rule and renaming Zaire the Democratic Republic of the Congo. Ghana’s Kofi Annan became UN secretary-general.
1997.india: India and Pakistan marked 50 years of independence. K.R. Narayanan became India’s first Dalit president, and Arundhati Roy won the Booker Prize for “The God of Small Things”.
1997.china: Deng Xiaoping died in February, and Britain handed Hong Kong back to China on 1 July. The Asian financial crisis began in Thailand and forced South Korea to seek an IMF bailout.

1999.us: The Senate acquitted President Clinton in his impeachment trial in February. Two students killed 13 people at Columbine High School, and protests disrupted the WTO meeting in Seattle.
1999.latam: Hugo Chávez became Venezuela’s president, and floods and mudslides in Vargas state killed thousands in December. The United States handed the Panama Canal to Panama on 31 December.
1999.europe: The euro launched on 1 January as an electronic currency in 11 countries. NATO bombed Yugoslavia for 78 days over Kosovo, and Poland, Hungary and the Czech Republic joined NATO.
1999.russia: Apartment bombings, which officials blamed on Chechen militants, killed about 300 people, and Russia launched a second war in Chechnya. Boris Yeltsin resigned on 31 December, naming Vladimir Putin acting president.
1999.mideast: Jordan’s King Hussein and Morocco’s King Hassan II died, and their sons took the thrones. An earthquake near İzmit, Turkey, killed about 17,000 people in August.
1999.africa: Nigeria returned to civilian rule under Olusegun Obasanjo, and Thabo Mbeki succeeded Nelson Mandela in South Africa. Sierra Leone’s government and rebels signed the Lomé peace accord.
1999.india: India and Pakistan fought the Kargil conflict in Kashmir’s mountains. General Pervez Musharraf seized power in Pakistan in October, and a super cyclone killed about 10,000 people in Orissa.
1999.china: Portugal handed Macau to China in December, and Beijing banned the Falun Gong movement. An earthquake killed about 2,400 people in Taiwan, and a nuclear accident struck Tokaimura, Japan.

2000.us: The presidential election came down to a Florida recount, halted by the Supreme Court in December, making George W. Bush the winner over Al Gore. The dot-com bubble burst.
2000.latam: Vicente Fox won Mexico’s presidency, ending 71 years of rule by the PRI. In Peru, Alberto Fujimori fled to Japan amid a corruption scandal and resigned by fax.
2000.europe: Mass protests in Belgrade toppled Slobodan Milošević in October. An Air France Concorde crashed near Paris in July, killing 113, and the new euro fell to record lows.
2000.russia: Vladimir Putin won the presidential election in March. In August, the submarine Kursk sank in the Barents Sea with all 118 aboard, and Putin faced criticism for his slow response.
2000.mideast: Israel withdrew from southern Lebanon, Camp David peace talks failed, and the Second Intifada began in September. Syria’s Hafez al-Assad died, and his son Bashar took power.
2000.africa: Floods devastated Mozambique, where a baby was born in a tree above the water. Zimbabwe began seizing white-owned farms, and British troops intervened in Sierra Leone’s civil war.
2000.india: India’s population passed one billion, and three new states were created: Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand and Uttaranchal, now Uttarakhand. Bill Clinton made the first US presidential visit in 22 years.
2000.china: Kim Dae-jung met Kim Jong-il in Pyongyang at the first inter-Korean summit and won the Nobel Peace Prize. In Taiwan, Chen Shui-bian’s election ended five decades of Kuomintang rule.

2003.us: The US led the invasion of Iraq in March. Space shuttle Columbia broke apart on re-entry in February, and Arnold Schwarzenegger was elected governor of California in a recall vote.
2003.latam: Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva became Brazil’s president, and Néstor Kirchner took office in Argentina. Deadly protests over gas exports forced Bolivia’s president to resign in October.
2003.europe: Millions marched against the Iraq war on 15 February. An August heatwave killed tens of thousands across Europe, about 15,000 in France alone, and Concorde made its last flights.
2003.russia: Oil tycoon Mikhail Khodorkovsky, Russia’s richest man, was arrested in October. Putin’s United Russia party won December’s parliamentary elections, and St Petersburg celebrated its 300th anniversary.
2003.mideast: US-led forces toppled Saddam Hussein in April and captured him in December. An earthquake destroyed Bam in Iran, killing about 26,000, and Libya agreed to abandon weapons of mass destruction.
2003.africa: Fighting in Sudan’s Darfur escalated as government-backed militias attacked civilians. In Liberia, Charles Taylor stepped down and went into exile in Nigeria as rebels besieged Monrovia.
2003.india: India and Pakistan agreed a ceasefire along the Line of Control in Kashmir in November. Twin car bombs killed more than 50 people in Mumbai in August.
2003.china: SARS spread from southern China, killing about 800 people worldwide. Hu Jintao became China’s president, and Yang Liwei became the country’s first astronaut in space.
